accuracy.evidence: Checked against the national curriculum in England, English Appendix 2 Year 5 (converting nouns or adjectives into verbs using the suffixes -ate, -ise, -ify) and the Oxford Learner's Dictionary entries for every lab verb: classify, finalise, sharpen, solidify, hyphenate, fossilise, simplify, apologise, activate, lengthen, memorise, pollinate, shorten, purify. The -en suffix is presented as an extra verb-forming suffix for some adjectives, not as one of the three curriculum suffixes. The e/y rule is stated as 'usually drops', since solid and length keep every letter; -ise and -ize are both given as correct British spellings.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips seen in Year 5 writing: any suffix on any root (classise, sharpify: prediction 1, BUILD feedback, challenge q2 and q6), keeping a final e or y (simpleify, apologyse, pureify: TRIM, FIX 1 and 3, challenge q1 and q4, m1 and m6), dropping a letter that should stay (TRIM solid and length with 'Keep every letter'), using the root where a verb is needed (the cold will solid the fat: FIX 4, JOB, m8), and thinking every verb was made with a suffix (needed in FIND 2 and m7).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmkverb is built on word-class conversion: a suffix tile is dragged onto a root and the slot shows whether the verb is real, the root is split into letter tiles so the learner taps the e or y that drops, a sentence gap is filled with root or verb by its grammatical job, the converted verb is found among other verbs, and a slip finder mixes suffix, spelling and word-class errors. flagsfxrule and flagvend teach -ing/-ed endings on verbs, not verb formation; lab_distinct gate is 9% or less against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The rules come out of the feedback: dropping -ise on class returns 'classise is not a word. Say each one aloud; class takes -ify'; keeping all letters in simple returns 'Keep it all and you get simpleify. The final e drops: simplify'; tapping i in simple says only the last letter drops; choosing pollinate after The says the gap needs a noun; tapping needed says it is a verb but no suffix made it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the task then disproves: 'yes, they all mean make' (BUILD rejects every wrong suffix), 'yes, never change the root' for simple + -ify (TRIM 1 needs the e dropped), and 'yes, the sentence is about pollen' for Bees ▢ the flowers (JOB 2 needs pollinate). A.reveal names the locked-in pick when each task ends.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with twelve wrong-answer messages naming the slip: drop the final e before -ify, pure takes -ify not -ise, hyphenify and hyphenen are not words, class is a noun after need to, class takes -ify, drop the y before -ise, the y must go, solid on its own is a describing word, solid describes a thing so it is an adjective, sharp is an adjective so the verb is sharpen, and sharp takes -en not -ify.

readability.evidence: learn/readability.py: kid FK grade 3.5 (family limit 5.0), adult 6.2 (limit 10.0). Kid paragraphs use one or two examples each (class/classify, simple/simplify, bees pollinate). Canvas instructions are one short sentence and feedback is one or two sentences.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs cover what a verb is, the four suffixes, one root one suffix, and the e/y drop with word class. Adult text gives the Year 5 Appendix 2 statement, how the job in the sentence changes, -ise/-ize, five named mistakes and what the lab does. Content gate found no filler; explanation under 12% similar to every other lesson including 777 spelling verb endings and 761 adjectives v adverbs.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark for all six steps plus a wrong-answer state on each task (classise, i tapped in simple, pollinate after The, cold tapped, Please tapped). The root and drop slot first clipped the slot on the right at 360 px; both boxes are now sized together and centred. Suffix tiles are at least 54 px tall. Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag and tap has a button below the canvas: one per suffix ('Add -ify to class'), one per letter plus Keep every letter ('Drop letter 6, e'), root and verb ('Use pollinate'), and one per word in the find and slip sentences. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action, the challenge feedback is a role=status live region, warnings switch to #fda4af on dark, and axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
